nodes.body: Hey @sagearc, this looks interesting! I’ve also recently been experimenting with `vllm-router` to reuse the Rust frontend’s upper-level layers, such as server, rendering, and parsing, which seems pretty similar to your idea. We probably don’t want to abstract the raw `EngineCoreClient`, but rather a higher-level component like `TextLlm`. I’ll let you know if there are any updates!

thanks @BugenZhao ! as far as i understand, the current flow is roughly:

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ChatLlm                                      │
│                                              │
│ Renders chat, tokenizes through              │
│ TextRequestProcessor, prepares output parser │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │ TextRequest with token IDs
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ TextLlm                                      │
│                                              │
│ Resolves sampling and lowers the request     │
│ Decodes returned tokens                      │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │ GenerateRequest
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Llm                                          │
│                                              │
│ Manages native request tracking              │
│ and cancellation                             │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │ EngineCoreRequest
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ EngineCoreClient                             │
│                                              │
│ Communicates with the engine through ZMQ     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

since the engine stays the same, i initially thought only the generation connection would differ. could you share what led you toward abstracting `TextLlm` itself?


also, could the frontend integration be reused independently of `vllm-router`, or enabled selectively through feature flags, similar to `sgl-router`?

After second thought I think you're right! I initially chose to abstract `TextLlm` mainly to align with the current `Generate` interface in `vllm-proto`, which Dynamo already uses as the boundary between router and worker. The main benefits of doing that were:

* vLLM still validates and normalizes the sampling parameters, so the internal `EngineCore` representation doesn't leak into the public interfaces in `vllm-proto`.
* The worker keeps the text layer, so it can detokenize and handle `stop_str` locally.

But it turns out that:

* `/inference/v1/generate` is already there as a boundary in pure token mode.
* The text layer is very valuable to keep on the frontend side, especially now that the vLLM Rust frontend detokenizes into text with per-token attributions instead of a plain string, which gives the parsers more information.
* `stop_str` can still be handled on the frontend side: on a match it just drops the stream, which aborts the request on the remote engine, at the cost of a few extra tokens.

> could the frontend integration be reused independently of `vllm-router`

Yes, that's the goal! What we want here is just a generic/remote version of `Llm`, so any system implementing that trait can integrate with the `server + chat + text` layers of the Rust frontend.
@BugenZhao Moved `EngineClient` below `Llm` now, let me know what you think

Hey @sagearc, sorry I wasn’t very clear earlier. Looking at it again, I actually think your original direction, i.e. abstracting Llm itself, is the better one and it seems we don’t need the control interfaces on it.

I’ve put together a version of that in #64695 and added you as a co-author. The trait is `vllm_llm::Llm` (info, health, generate, abort, shutdown), where today’s `Llm` struct becomes `EngineCoreLlm`, and `TextLlm` now holds a `Box<dyn Llm>`. I also saw your branch at https://github.com/sagearc/vllm/tree/backup/rust-engine-http-client-20261029, and I think this can support it.

Could you take a look and see whether this works for you? Your HTTP client could then go on top of it.

Oh this branch is not up to date with the current revision, my local branch has drifted a lot since :) I can share it, the backup branch indeed assumed the abstraction at the Llm struct. Thanks anyways!
I'll take a look at #64695

merged. Please rebase the PR, @sagearc.
